# Njenga Kariuki

> AI executive leading enterprise AI transformation across Vodacom FinTech Group, including M-PESA Africa, serving 100M+ customers across eight African markets and $2B+ revenue, reporting to the CEO and building the AI Center of Excellence. Previously spent 12 years in the United States at Amazon/AWS building and scaling AI-native businesses and products from zero to one across software, hardware, and mobile applications spanning e-commerce, IoT, connected devices, supply chain, health, and life sciences, leading science, engineering, and product organizations of 100+, directing $100M+ AI portfolios and businesses up to $700M, and delivering frontier ML, computer vision, and LLM capabilities at global scale (most recently leading product for Amazon Bio Discovery, an agentic AI platform for drug discovery). Holds a Master of Science in Management from Stanford Graduate School of Business, published research on AI's global economic impact at the Stanford Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence (Stanford HAI, AI Index Report 2025), and is a named inventor on six U.S. patents.

Identity: This is the Njenga Kariuki (AI executive and product leader) of https://njenga.ai/, https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q142243592, https://orcid.org/0009-0003-8191-2625, https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=v-VqXH0AAAAJ, https://www.crunchbase.com/person/njenga-kariuki, https://www.linkedin.com/in/njengakariuki/, https://github.com/njenga-kariuki, and https://patents.justia.com/inventor/njenga-kariuki.

## Facts

- Current role: Managing Executive: AI at M-PESA Africa, Vodacom FinTech Group (Nairobi, Kenya, 2026–today), reporting to the CEO. Owns the enterprise AI roadmap for customer experience, revenue growth, risk, fraud, and operational efficiency, and is building the AI Center of Excellence across eight markets: Kenya, Tanzania, Ethiopia, the DRC, Mozambique, Lesotho, South Africa, and Egypt.
- Operating approach: Leads AI transformation at two levels, setting strategy with the CEO and executive team, and building hands-on in the forward-deployed engineer's role; moves AI from isolated single-function tasks (units of work) to cross-functional chains redesigned end to end (systems of work), measured against comparison groups.
- Amazon/AWS (United States, 2014–2026): Head of Product, AWS Applied AI, Life Sciences, led product for Amazon Bio Discovery, an agentic AI application for antibody design (launched 14 April 2026), directing 100+ engineers, scientists, and product managers; Senior Manager TPM, Alexa Smart Home & Map View (50M+ monthly app users); Principal TPM & first product lead of Amazon's Health Computer Vision and AI organization (100+ scientists/engineers, $100M+/yr portfolio); founding team & product lead for Amazon Halo (Body, Tone, Movement); first product lead for Alexa Shopping NLU; founding PM of Prime Now's local-store platform; Vendor Manager, Amazon Bedding & Bath ($100M+ P&L).
- Before Amazon (United States, 2012–2014): Senior Supply Chain Analyst for Target's $700M+/yr Apple category across ~1,800 U.S. stores.
- Intellectual property & research: Six granted U.S. patents (Halo Tone voice AI, 2022–2026); three peer-reviewed clinical validation studies in npj Digital Medicine of products he led (2022, 2022, 2023); author of Chapter 4 (Economy) of Stanford HAI's AI Index Report 2025 (cited by the U.S. Federal Reserve Board and White House Council of Economic Advisers).
- Hands-on builds on GitHub (2025–2026): https://github.com/njenga-kariuki

## Across Africa

- Scale: Vodacom FinTech Group, including M-PESA Africa (jointly established by Safaricom and Vodacom in 2020): 100M+ customers and $2B+ revenue.
- Mandate: Enterprise AI strategy, AI Center of Excellence governance and training standards, and cross-functional workflow redesign across regulated financial services with legal, risk, and compliance sign-off.
- Speaking: Headline fireside chat at Africa Tech Festival 2026 (Cape Town, 17 November 2026), "Beyond Adoption: What Will Make Africa an AI Producer, Not Just a Consumer?", moderated by Loni Prinsloo (Bloomberg).

## Signature Frameworks & Published Analysis

In his November 2026 essay, [Africa’s Hidden AI Bottleneck](https://njenga.ai/writing/africa-ai-bottleneck/) (1,761 words, 2 figures, 12 sources, 7 min read), Njenga Kariuki argues that Africa lacks a shared, testable definition of what good AI looks like under local conditions, and sets out six points relevant to African AI strategy, sovereign AI policy, and enterprise AI execution:

- **The hidden bottleneck (#thesis, #builders):** Alongside power, compute, local data, capital, and talent sits a constraint that is harder to see: no shared, testable definition of good AI. In a survey of 85 African AI businesses, the barrier named most was customer trust and AI literacy (about two in three named it). Buyers cannot tell what will work, and builders cannot tell what test they have to pass.
- **Private evaluations: a test for each workflow (#workflow-tests):** An organization codifies its most important workflows and builds a private test for each one: real cases from its own work, the result its best people would accept, and what that work costs today. The organization runs the test, and any supplier can take it. Alexa Shopping, 2017–2018: the share of requests that ended in the right offer rose from about 50% to 85%.
- **Shared African AI benchmarks (#shared-benchmarks):** Industries, NGOs, and governments agree on benchmarks for the conditions they have in common, built with the method of OpenAI’s GDPval, for the work that drives African economies: mobile money and small-merchant credit, primary care, smallholder farming, classroom teaching.
- **What to buy, and what to build and own: the five-layer AI stack (#buy-build-own):** *“If it gets cheaper without us, buy it, and stay free to switch. If it depends on our data and knowledge, build it, and own it.”* Across five layers of the AI stack: build applications, delivery, and knowledge, and own the knowledge and the evaluations; buy general models and build small ones for local languages and phones; build the computing that has to run locally, as demand arrives. AI sovereignty means owning the definition of good, controlling the data and knowledge, keeping the right to verify and switch models, and running critical work locally.
- **Two questions for leaders (#two-questions):** For enterprise leaders: if a small local team built something better next week, how long would it take you to know, and then to sign? For public leaders, funders, and their partners: if a local team passed a shared benchmark next month, do your procurement rules give it a path to scale?
- **AI skills and jobs: the people who build the tests (#people, #stakes):** Building a definition of good is skilled work. Between May and July 2026, four of the largest AI suppliers announced about US$9 billion to place engineers inside their customers’ organizations. The people who build an organization’s definition of good should be its own people, trained in Africa. By 2050, more than three in four net additions to the world’s working-age population will be in Sub-Saharan Africa.
